title: A look at Fortune, Fame & Glory - A free PnP Adventure Game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=afLeJEbZs2k

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at *Fortune, Fame & Glory*, a free print-and-play adventure game by Joseph Mills (of Ganesha Games and *Four Against Darkness* work, with an *Alone Against the Weird West* book promised) and art by Jason Glover, Glover's second appearance in a row on the channel. Daniel printed the cards on plain paper and slipped them into Frazetta-backed sleeves, the same deck he uses for his *Talisman* house rules.

The game is *Escape the Dark Castle* simple: lay the encounter deck in a ten-column diamond, start at the left, and flip a card per step, choosing north or south as the map widens. Three crossings, then a random final boss: a guarded artifact, a treasure hoard, or the Dark One with nineteen health and triple damage on a six. Combat is Fighting Fantasy style, both sides rolling a d6 plus a bonus, higher wins, one damage. Fate points nudge a die by two, gold turns up here and there, and every four cards you eat one food or lose a health (Daniel would prefer five, since a crossing is ten cards). Followers join for three cards and roll their own dice; his warrior helped skewer a skeleton before the swamp leeches got her.

His journey ran from a night attack through prison, sewers, friendly barbarians and a night at the inn. Not much strategy, not many choices, but for the price of ink and a rainy afternoon he finds it hard not to recommend.

----

What is the most fun you have had with a print-and-play that cost you nothing but paper and ink?
